title: Fit Check Sheet
summary: Sheet 09 of the drawing set takes 'fit' literally. A 1px isometric of the three-piece Kelwin mark is seated inside a dashed clearance envelope, its pieces lettered A–C and keyed to the three FIT criteria, beside a mirrored FIT | DECLINE spec table. A single red tag reads 'Gate · 3 of 3 required to seat'. Qualification becomes an engineering tolerance instead of a HUD schematic.

reference.borrowed: Speakeasy's framed comparison panel. Faint frame lines run past the panel's edges. A large two-line title sits top-left, with a drawing field beside it. Below, a band of bordered cells has a description cell on the left and then two equal bordered columns, each opened by a status header cell ('Where teams struggle' / 'How Speakeasy helps'), with ruled row cells read across as pairs.
reference.kelwin: The panel becomes a C paper document sheet. Frame verticals run at x 64/1376, the sheet opens on a --line-2 rule, and crosshairs sit at only three intersections. The serif title becomes the 88px uppercase 'NOT FOR / EVERYONE. / BY DESIGN.' (turn in --fg-3), set flush bottom-left in a 384px cols 1–8 title cell under a red-square sheet label, closed by the founder's 48×2 red rule. A cols 9–12 note cell holds the light 24px lede over the red 'C9·R3 · Fit verified in the audit / INITIATE SYSTEM AUDIT ↗' and bordered 'CONTACT →' action cells. Speakeasy's dot-art becomes FIG. 9.1, a 1px exact-30° isometric of the mark's three pieces (K1–K3, master proportions, hidden lines removed) seated in a dashed clearance envelope, with an envelope dimension and lettered callouts A–C on orthogonal leaders. The status-icon columns become two spec tables of cells: [+] FIT · 03 'All required' and [−] DECLINE · 03 'Any one declines'. Their F-/D- rows are paired by axis (Stage · Ownership · Motion) with no green and no icons, and the FIT rows carry the A–C keys. The sheet's one red element besides the action cell is the gate tag on a leader from the envelope. A mono legend and the title block close the sheet.

motion: entrance, in drafting order (--ease-inout, no overshoot): the frame verticals and crosshairs fade in (300ms). Cell borders draw in raster order (440ms each, 40ms stagger). The red label square appears, the three title lines wipe in one after another (100ms apart) and the red rule draws. The note and action cells fade in, and mono IDs, headers, legend and title block type on at 24ms per character.

the orchestrated moment, the fit check (~1.1–3.5s): the construction grid and the dashed envelope fade in. The assembly then plots one piece at a time, A (the core), then B, then C, 400ms apart, each by stroke-dashoffset. Each piece's faces fill once its outline closes, so the hidden lines behind it drop out. As each piece seats, its lettered callout drops in on its leader, the matching F-row key pings (ink fill, 700ms), and the 'Seated' readout ticks 0/3 → 1/3 → 2/3 → 3/3. The envelope dimension then draws, and the red gate tag settles last on its leader (opacity + 8px, 400ms).

interaction: hovering a FIT row turns its lettered callout, leader and key --accent. Hovering a DECLINE row inverts its cell ID. The action cells invert on hover (audit to --accent-hover, contact to --fg fill).
on the live site: the fit check runs once when the sheet is 50% in view. Reduced motion shows the fully plotted final state, Seated 3/3.
notes: Numbered SHEET 09/14 to follow method's SHEET 08/14 (C sheets elsewhere: nav 00, hero 01, reframe 02, architecture 05, statechange 06, method 08). The research plan suggested 10/14, but 09 keeps the sequence unbroken. The drawing uses the corrected three-piece mark (K1–K3 at the 152-unit master proportions), extruded 20U inside a 176U envelope (12U clearance), so A–C map one-to-one to F-01…F-03. Decline rows are reordered to mirror their FIT pair by axis. The third crosshair sits at the drawing/table/title joint (x 497, y 384) rather than the title/note joint, which the red action cell covers. The title row is 384px (as in method-C) to carry the 88px three-line title, so the sheet is 1008px tall.
